statusText: Mapped policy state: WATCH. Tail risk of 20% sits at the lower edge of the watch band, five points below the 25% block threshold.
recommendation: Tail remains below the block threshold, so the mapped policy state is WATCH. The evidence-based danger window runs from the 12:30Z September employment report through 15:00Z, covering post-release repricing, the 13:30Z cash open and the first full cash hour. Existing-position management and emergency protection are unaffected by this mapping.
headline: NQ holds 74 points under an unchanged 31,035 high as both Treasury yields turn lower 58 minutes before the September payrolls print
body:
NQ futures trade 30,961.75 (+201.25, +0.65%) on a delayed CME quote timed 11:16:48Z, inside a session range of 30,760.25-31,035.25 against a 30,760.50 prior settlement, from a 30,771.25 open on about 91.7k contracts. The decisive observation this hour is that the 31,035.25 session high has not advanced at all: it stood at the same level an hour ago, and price now sits roughly 74 points, or 0.24%, beneath it. Extension has therefore moved from stalling to fully flat, and the retracement that formed in the previous hour has held rather than failed. Holding near the session extreme was the one live Tail amplifier in the preceding assessments and it remains absent for a second consecutive hour. The prior hour's own forecast carried 21% for this slot on the expectation that pre-release depth would thin; the observed evidence came in more benign than that conditional path, so the published level eases to 20% at the lower edge of the watch band instead.

Cross-asset evidence has moved further away from, not toward, an aligned one-way equity path. The 10-year Treasury yield is 5.229%, down 0.009 from a 5.238% close inside a 5.221-5.262 range, and the 2-year is 4.781% against a 4.787% close in a 4.775-4.804 band. Both were marginally higher an hour ago and are now lower on the day, which removes the mild cross-asset conflict noted previously and leaves the long end about 11.5 basis points under Thursday's 5.344% print, the highest 10-year yield since 2002. VIX is 15.99, down 2.44% from a 16.39 close and in the lower half of a 15.89-16.24 band. WTI is 89.30, down 3.84% from 92.87 and near a 88.92 session low after trading as high as 93.51, with Brent reported in a 97-102 dollar band since late September; falling crude is a disinflationary offset rather than a Tail amplifier. S&P 500 futures at 7,762.00 (+0.49%) sit only 3.75 points under their own 7,765.75 high, so the broad index is closer to its extreme than NQ is. That is a mild intra-equity divergence, and because NQ futures are the preferred price-discovery reference under this contract, the Nasdaq-100 instrument's own confirmed retracement governs the reading.

The dominant scheduled catalyst has not yet printed. The September employment report is released at 12:30Z, 58 minutes after this assessment, with consensus near +84-85k payrolls, unemployment held at 4.1% and average hourly earnings around 3.1-3.2% year on year. Under this provider's risk definition, event importance, forecast dispersion and surprise magnitude inform Stress and Confidence rather than Tail until an observed price path establishes mean-reversion failure, so no part of the current 20% reading anticipates the release. Rate-path pricing frames the release: October hike odds have fallen to roughly 34% from about 70% a week earlier, while most traders still carry at least one 25 basis point hike by December. Thursday's cash session supports the mean-reverting read directly, with the Nasdaq-100 closing 30,501.56 (+0.31%) after trading 30,274.65-30,616.24, giving back more than half its range into the close while the 10-year retreated from its multidecade high. Micron's fourth-quarter beat and raised first-quarter outlook remain the active semiconductor catalyst behind that advance and behind Thursday's broad Asian chip rally. Geopolitical transmission is currently absent despite an eighth-month Middle East war, reported additional U.S. deployments to the Persian Gulf and EU deliberations over a strategic reserve release, because crude is falling rather than rising into the weekend.

Stress eases one point to 75% in the high band. Easing yields and a sharply lower crude price reduce two of the three active stress channels, while a Tier-1 release inside the next hour and a 10-year still near 5.23% keep the environment difficult. Confidence holds at 88%. The evidence set is broad and current: a timed NQ quote with full range and volume, a cross-checked ES reading, direct 2-year and 10-year yields with intraday ranges, VIX and WTI with ranges, the verified cash close, verified release timings and verified reporting on the semiconductor and crude narratives. Two limitations are recorded rather than smoothed over. The shared Finviz context file is unusable this run: its collection timestamp is 2026-09-29T23:14:22Z, nearly three days past the 90-minute freshness limit, its collection status is partial, and its calendar and futures sections are flagged unavailable, so it contributed nothing and full independent research was performed in its place. Separately, the third-party economic calendar used for event timing rendered an actual-value column populated for releases that have not yet occurred, including this session's payrolls print and events as far out as 9 October; every one of those values was discarded as a source defect and only the event timings, which match independently verified reporting, were used.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding published Claude hours stayed inside the watch band. Tail entered the window at 20% in the 11:00Z hour on 1 October, peaked at 24% during the 14:00Z hour as long-end selling intensified, then printed 20% for thirteen consecutive hours across the U.S. afternoon and the Asian session before stepping to 21% at 07:00Z, 23% at 08:00Z and 22% at 09:00Z as the European-morning advance gained directional efficiency, and returning to 20% at 10:00Z once a genuine retracement formed. Stress ranged from 74% to a 79% overnight peak and closed the window at 76%; Confidence held between 87% and 89%. Only the 08:00Z and 09:00Z slots were published as trend-up; every other hour in the window was mixed.
outlookSummary: The forecast holds Tail at 20% for the current hour on the confirmed retracement and the unchanged session high, then steps to 24% in the 12:00Z hour containing the 12:30Z employment report. It reaches the 25% block threshold only for the 13:00Z and 14:00Z slots covering post-release repricing, the 13:30Z cash open and the first full cash hour. That elevation is conditional on an aligned opening auction, pullbacks that fail and a long-end move back toward Thursday's 5.344% peak; it is not an assertion that such a path has formed, and a confirmed retracement inside those hours would invalidate it. Tail then eases through the afternoon as repricing is assumed to complete, with a small uplift to 22% for the 19:00Z power hour, before returning to the 20% watch floor at the 20:00Z cash close. CME equity index futures halt for the weekend at 21:00Z, so the final fourteen slots are an explicitly carried 20% floor rather than a projection of structure: no price path can form inside a closed market. Stress peaks at 83% in the extreme band across the release and cash open, decays through the afternoon and settles on a 60% weekend floor held deliberately above a quiet-market reading because the elevated long-end backdrop and the active Middle East conflict persist across the halt. Confidence steps down from 88% to 74% with distance from the evidence cutoff.
